opening.quote: Agent: Yeah, hello, how can I help?
opening.comment: The agent greeted the caller but did not give their own name or the company name, so the opening criterion is not met.

verification.comment: The agent asked for full name and order number or postcode and the caller gave both before account details were discussed, so this is met.

understanding.quote: Agent: Thank ya, Mark. I can see the order for a pair of cushions at €64.90, and two payments on the same day. So you need the second €64.90 back?
understanding.comment: The agent captured the duplicate charge issue correctly, though it addressed the caller as Mark when the caller said their name was Mike, which is a confusing error.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Agent: I've refunded €46.90 to your today. It'll show within 3 to 5 so working days.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The refund amount was wrong: the duplicate charge was €64.90, so the agent should have refunded €64.90, not €46.90.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: You'll get a confirmation email shortly. Anything else I can help with?
process_compliance.comment: No hold occurred and no bank dispute or damage process applied, so the applicable steps were followed.

communication.quote: Agent: Sorry about the, I know that's stressful to see on your statement.
communication.comment: The agent was polite and acknowledged the caller's stress about the duplicate charge, though it misnamed the caller as Mark.

closing.quote: Agent: Thanks for calling, Mark, take care.
closing.comment: The agent asked if there was anything else and closed politely, but the next step was stated only vaguely and the wrong name was used.
